project: Pointed Order Zeta: Artin–Kummer Spectra of Reduction Orders
frozen_definitions: Initial base a is a nonzero integer, a != ±1, initially not a perfect power.
For primes p not dividing a, ord_p(a) is the multiplicative order of a modulo p.
Residual index: I_a(p) = (p - 1) / ord_p(a) = [F_p^x : <a mod p>].
Starting Euler product: Z_a(s,z) = product_{p not dividing a} (1 - I_a(p)^(-z) p^(-s))^(-1).
Initial rigorous domain: real z >= 0 and Re(s) > 1; no analytic continuation is assumed in the definition.
Provisional mean: Delta_a(z) = lim_{x->infinity} (1/pi(x)) sum_{p<=x, p not dividing a} I_a(p)^(-z), whenever the limit exists.
Kummer fields: K_n(a) = Q(zeta_n, a^(1/n)), subject to perfect-power and entanglement caveats.
foundational_results: For n >= 1 and p not dividing a: n | I_a(p) iff n | (p-1) and a mod p is an n-th power in F_p^x.
For fixed n and p not dividing a*n: n | I_a(p) iff p splits completely in K_n(a)=Q(zeta_n,a^(1/n)).
For any arithmetic f, f(I_a(p)) = sum_{n | I_a(p)} (mu*f)(n), pointwise finitely.
For f_z(n)=n^(-z), g_z=mu*f_z is multiplicative and g_z(q^k)=q^(-kz)-q^(-(k-1)z).
For z >= 0 and Re(s)>1, log Z_a(s,z) is absolutely convergent.
prior_art_results: Residual index and fixed exact-index distributions are standard generalized-Artin/near-primitive-root objects.
Felix-Murty (2012), Theorem 1.7, gives under GRH fixed-base weighted asymptotics for broad f(i_a(p)) with Kummer-degree constant sum g(n)/[K_n(a):Q].
For each fixed real z>0, |g_z(n)|<=1, so Delta_a(z) is an immediate specialization of Felix-Murty in the paper's standing positive-base setup.
Wagstaff's degree formula, reproduced in Felix-Murty Proposition 3.3, gives [K_n(a):Q] asymptotic_a n*phi(n) with explicit corrections.
Akbary-Fakhari develops product/entanglement structure for generalized-Artin constants.
No direct primary source was located in Session 3 for the exact two-variable product Z_a(s,z); nonappearance is not a novelty claim.
session4_analytic_results: For real z>=0, R_a(s,z)=sum_p sum_{k>=2} I_a(p)^(-zk)/(k p^(ks)) is holomorphic for Re(s)>1/2 by locally uniform absolute convergence.
Writing P(s)=sum_p p^(-s) and Q_a(s,z)=P_a(s,z)-Delta_a(z)P(s), one has exactly for Re(s)>1: log H_a(s,z)=Q_a(s,z)+R_a(s,z)-Delta_a(z)R_zeta(s).

For source-matched positive a and fixed real z>0, Felix-Murty gives under GRH an error O(x/(log x)^beta) for every fixed beta<2. After subtracting Delta_a(z) pi(x), partial summation gives a finite continuous boundary value of Q_a(s,z) on Re(s)=1.
More quantitatively, for every fixed gamma<1 the same error gives Q_a(1+delta,z)-Q_a(1,z)=O(delta^gamma) as delta->0+, but it does not imply differentiability at the boundary.

Consequently, under those GRH hypotheses, H_a(s,z)=Z_a(s,z) zeta(s)^(-Delta_a(z)) has a finite positive real limit as s->1+, and Z_a(s,z) is asymptotic to C_a(z)(s-1)^(-Delta_a(z)). This is Level 1 only.

The Felix-Murty logarithmic error does not imply differentiability at s=1 or holomorphic continuation into any half-plane Re(s)<1. A power-saving error would be needed for such Mellin continuation by this route.
For real z>0 and Re(s)>1, the Kummer-indicator expansion may be interchanged absolutely with the prime sum; the divisor-support bound sum_{n|I}|g_z(n)| <= tau(I) supplies the convergence mechanism.

At each fixed Kummer level, the completely-split prime series admits an exact finite-Galois character decomposition into logarithms of Artin L-functions, equivalently (1/[K:Q]) log zeta_K(s), plus ramified and prime-power corrections holomorphic for Re(s)>1/2.

The naive infinite tower obtained by separating those finite-level L-function expressions is not justified by degree growth alone: the divisor-support cancellation/convergence is lost after separation.
For positive non-perfect-power a, the Kummer degree series sum g_z(n)/[K_n(a):Q] converges absolutely and locally uniformly for complex z with Re(z)>-1; no complex-z prime-mean theorem is claimed.
session4_computation: Extended the exact Session-2 engine with sieve-backed factorization, prime generation, residual-index tables, prime Dirichlet sums, logarithmic Euler products, matched-cutoff normalization, and the source-matched positive non-perfect-power degree formula.
Default pilot cutoffs are X=1000000 and N=500000 for bases 2,3,5,6,10 and z in {0,1/2,1,2,4,8}; all exact arithmetic tests pass.
At X=1000000 and N=500000, empirical prime means and Kummer-degree predictions typically agree at about 1e-4 to 1e-3; a=10 is slower, near 2e-3 in several displayed cases.

Matched-cutoff normalized logarithms are stable across X=10000,100000,1000000 to about 1e-3 in the tested family. Combining finite Z_X with full zeta(s) produces misleading omitted-prime-tail bias near s=1.
No stable secondary term, simple new constant, or numerical evidence for Level-2/Level-3 continuation was found.

open_questions: Can one prove a tower-averaged power-saving estimate for sum_{n<=N} g_z(n)(pi_n(x)-li(x)/[K_n(a):Q]) with N=x^alpha for some alpha>0?
Can the prime-supported large-divisor tail sum_{p<=x} sum_{n|I_a(p), n>N} g_z(n) be centered and bounded by O(x^(1-delta)) for a power-sized N?
Is there a large-sieve-for-Frobenius, zero-density, or explicit-formula theorem genuinely uniform for this nested unbounded-degree Kummer family that supplies cancellation across n?
Can a smoothed version of the tower discrepancy be proved with a power saving and then converted into Level-2 or Level-3 continuation of Q_a?
Could Q_a(s,z) continue across Re(s)=1 for reasons not visible in the separated Kummer tower?
Does Felix-Murty Theorem 1.7, or a later theorem of equal generality, explicitly cover negative integer bases for general f(i_a(p))?

session5_proof_results: The analytically clean proof object is the omitted-prime centered series Q_a^circ(s,z)=sum_{p not dividing a}(I_a(p)^(-z)-Delta_a(z))p^(-s), which differs from Q_a by a finite entire Dirichlet polynomial.
For Re(s)>1, Q_a^circ has an exact absolutely convergent centered Kummer expansion sum_n g_z(n)(S_{a,n}(s)-P_a^circ(s,0)/[K_n(a):Q]).
For a finite Galois K/Q, centering deletes the trivial regular-character contribution exactly: C_K(s)=(1/[K:Q]) log(zeta_K(s)/zeta(s))-B_K(s), with B_K holomorphic for Re(s)>1/2.

Aramata-Brauer makes zeta_K/zeta entire and nonzero at s=1. Thus each fixed centered Chebotarev level continues through a K-dependent neighborhood of s=1 unconditionally; under Dedekind GRH it is holomorphic on Re(s)>1/2.
For positive non-perfect-power a, log |Disc(K_n(a))| <= [K_n(a):Q](3 log n + log a), and the root discriminant is at most a*n^3.
Under GRH for zeta_{K_n(a)}, Felix-Murty/Serre gives pi_n(x)=li(x)/[K_n(a):Q]+O_a(sqrt(x) log(nx)), uniformly with explicit n-dependence.
On compact subsets of Re(s)>1/2, the centered finite-level series satisfies C_{K_n(a)}(s)=O_{a,Omega}(log(2n)). This bound is not summable against g_z because |g_z(q)|=1-q^(-z) tends to 1 on prime q.

A finite tower n<=N has GRH error O_a(sqrt(x) N log(Nx)); the Kummer-degree mean tail is polynomially small in N, but the prime-supported large-divisor tail is controlled by the source-matched Felix-Murty argument only at logarithmic scale.

The formal balance N=x^(1/4) would put the finite Chebotarev error and degree mean tail near x^(3/4+o(1)), but no power-saving estimate is available for the corresponding divisor-supported prime tail. This is a proof-planning heuristic, not a theorem.
The logarithmic derivative removes branch bookkeeping at finite level but does not improve tower convergence or the n-dependence.
No Level-2 or Level-3 continuation of the full Q_a(s,z) was proved. No natural-boundary claim was made.
